Contract status

FHP contract status
StatusReleased contract. schemaVersion "1.1" shipped in shared specification v0.5.0 on 2026-11-04.
Versions this schema accepts1.0, 1.1. A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state any earlier minor of the same major, and holds each of them to that minor: what a later minor allows is invalid in an earlier one.
What it describesFHP is the FAIR-bioHeaders header for a protein FASTA file: a predicted proteome, a set taken from a protein database, or a curated set that combines both. It works exactly like FHR — ;~ YAML lines at the top of the file, one SHA-512/256 checksum over the exact bytes, a small required set and everything else optional — plus standalone JSON or YAML.
What it does not coverFHP records asserted provenance: what the set is, which species it belongs to, where the sequences came from, which software and protocol produced them, what it derives from by checksum, and what the producer measured about it. It is not a quality-control report, and no tool recomputes anything from the sequences.

Serializations with verified support

  • Protein FASTA with a ;~ header block, under the shared FORMAT.md rules. Header handling is alphabet-independent: stops, U, O, B, Z, J, X and lower case are ordinary bytes.
  • Standalone JSON and YAML metadata files.
  • Canonical JSON-LD with the reviewed FHP context (loss-preserving, no schema.org export profile) and standalone HTML microdata with the FHP itemtype — never the FHR itemtype.
  • No x- extension field survives a JSON-LD or microdata round trip: writers omit them (J9, M5).

Tools that implement this contract

  • fair-bioheaders 0.9.0 (PyPI) bundles the v0.5.0 FHP schema and reads and writes FHP 1.1, including extension fields, across combine, verify, validate, convert, strip, verify-links and assess.
  • The browser table builder on this site validates against its documented v0.4.0 snapshot (schemaVersion 1.0), not v0.5.0. Tracked in fair-bioheaders.github.io#15.
  • bioheaders verify-links FILE PARENT... checks each derivedFrom item against candidate parent files by recomputing their checksums.

Schema location

  • Fixed schema URL of the current release: https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhp/v0.5.0. Cite the release a record targets: never hard-code a "latest" schema, and never check an unknown version against a different one.
  • The same bytes at the release tag: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/v0.5.0/fhp.json, also fixed at commit 170e677fbb.
  • Development URL on main, the current contract, which moves: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/main/fhp.json.
  • Schema-version registry: schemas/versions.json and docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md.

Field reference

Every field of the contract appears here, including the fields and objects inherited from the shared core: nothing is left out because another type also uses it. Required means the key must be present; when present, requires lists the members that become mandatory once you supply an optional object. Constraints are reproduced verbatim from the schema, so a pattern you see here is the pattern the validator matches. Examples are the values stated by the released example records, which are synthetic, or an illustrative value where no example reaches the field.

Top-level fields

Every field of an FHP record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, with the single exception of the x- extension fields listed last.

x-<name>Optionalany JSON valuesingle value or array, at any depth
  • pattern: ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$

Extension field (rule R15): a top-level key the standard does not define, holding any value the producer needs.

Valid from FHP 1.1. Every other unknown key stays invalid, nested objects stay closed, and an x- key in a record that states 1.0 is rejected.

Use a namespace, x-<project>-<field>. Extension fields never override a standard field, are covered by the checksum, and are omitted from JSON-LD and microdata (J9, M5).

Records that cite a v0.4.x schema URL are checked against the v0.4.x schema, where an x- key is an unknown key, so files with extension fields cite v0.5.0 or later.

x-synthetic-reviewStatus: curatedillustrative value

Rules beyond a single field

FHP conditional and object-level rules, read from the schema bytes.
RuleWhat the contract requires
Extension fields need the newer minorThe schema rejects extension fields in a record that states schemaVersion: '1.0', so a 1.0 record keeps exactly its 1.0 outcome. A record using an extension states 1.1 or a later minor.
No key may contain a line feedpropertyNames rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.
The record is a closed objectadditionalProperties: false — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way.
Extension fields (rule R15)Top-level keys matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ are accepted (rule R15, docs/FORMAT.md) from FHP 1.1, released in shared specification v0.5.0.

What the schema cannot say

The contract is more than its JSON Schema. These requirements are normative for a conforming record, and a validator that cannot check them must say so:

  • proteome: "", taxon: {} and metadataAuthor: [] pass the released schema yet describe nothing: conforming required values are non-empty (docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md).
  • format: date and format: uri must be asserted by a conforming validator; a bare draft 2020-12 validator ignores them.
  • source[], sequenceStats, completeness and source[].assemblyAccession are producer assertions. Nothing here is verified against the sequences, and a checksum never authenticates an author.
  • FHP was first released in shared specification v0.4.0, so it has no legacy numeric schemaVersion compatibility path like FHR's rule V6.

Generated from fhp.json of FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification at v0.5.0 (commit 170e677fbb), byte-identical to the copy pinned at scripts/schema-snapshots/fhp-v0.5.0.json — SHA-256 2409739d4a223164ca368f93afa78c8f1e3809fb04ec46cc9a793cc5aaaba427. It documents 62 fields: 26 at the top level and 36 inside 9 nested or reused objects. Regenerate and compare with python3 scripts/schema_fields.py --check, which the site checks run on every pull request. The specification repository stays the authority: this page is a rendering of it, not a second definition.
